summary: Round-6 majors are both discharged and I re-derived them independently rather than accepting the text. The anchor is now a REFUSAL by the successor with the checkpoint inversion as its corroborating half, and it names my seed-the-pods-map-at-write-time mutation verbatim. The everyDeltas=1 claim is deleted and the RED measurement recorded; I re-derived the RED from the fixture (everyDeltas=1, successor commits podb 0, so the last checkpoint is {podb=0} and gains poda=42 only with the fold), so the fixture discriminates with no K change. Every factual claim about the tree verified: ChainEntry.VERSION_DELTA=0 / VERSION_KINDED=1 with CommitDelta.encode selecting on segments.size(); `new BatchingSequencer` appears only in three test files; CheckpointWriterContentTest:156 carries the doesNotContainKey tripwire and :128 the 9-then-4 Math::max test; ChainReplay:441 folds with Math::max; Invariants:116,253 use delta.runs(); Sequencer's javadoc defines the return as matched by submitted segment key; DefaultIngest:63,349 is the sole issuance site incrementing unconditionally; FaultInjectingStore.Faults carries ambiguousPut and duplicatePut; CheckpointCursor.newest:72-81 propagates Checkpoint.decode's IOException. One major remains, and it is the round-6 fix applied to only one of the two things sitting in the conditional row.

findings.location: docs/internal/product/backlog-notes.md:M4.10c block, the paragraph beginning "If a field is needed, `CommitDelta` and `Checkpoint` must agree on the key's SHAPE"
findings.title: The pre-upgrade checkpoint window is guarded only by M4.10c, the row that may be void -- and the mutation that breaks it is a NO-FORMAT-CHANGE one, so it lands precisely in the branch where M4.10c does not exist
findings.failure_scenario: MUTATION THAT SURVIVES EVERY ANCHOR NAMED: qualify the pod key INSIDE the existing String of Checkpoint.pods (Map<String,Long>) -- "poda" becomes "poda@e7", using the lease epoch the parent M4.10 row itself calls "the obvious candidate". No format changes: Checkpoint.VERSION stays 0, Checkpoint.decode:151 still compares equal, golden/checkpoint-v0.bin still round-trips, golden/chain-delta-v0.bin and chain-delta-batched-v1.bin are untouched, and every assertion in CheckpointWriterContentTest still holds because its fixtures are written post-change. M4.10b's answer is then legitimately "no formats change", M4.10c is VOID by its own banner, and the hazard has no row at all. On the first deploy, every checkpoint written by the previous version carries BARE keys; the window recovered by M4.10d's fold matches nothing; the dedup silently degrades to accepting every replay -- at exactly the moment the process restarted, which is the fault the whole task exists to fix. THE ROW ALSO STATES THE WRONG FAILURE DIRECTION for this case: it says the mismatch makes "post-restart flushSeq 0 match pre-restart flushSeq 0", i.e. a real commit SUPPRESSED. For a pre-upgrade checkpoint the mismatch means NOTHING matches, i.e. a real replay ACCEPTED TWICE. A session that reads the row and covers the suppression direction will close it believing the acceptance direction is covered. This is structurally the same defect round 6 fixed by moving the end-to-end anchor out of the conditional row so a "no format change" finding could not take it down -- applied to the anchor and not to compatibility, in the same commit. REMEDY, additive and re-opening no prose that has been wrong before: a sixth bullet in M4.10b's property list (the unconditional, first-picked row), saying that a window recovered from an object written by the PREVIOUS version must still match, or the ADR must say the window is deliberately dropped on upgrade and why that is safe -- and that qualifying the key inside Checkpoint.pods's existing String field is a key-shape change even though it is not a format change. Answering the parent's question directly: this must NOT be deferred to M4.10c when that row is picked up, because the mutation is exactly the one under which M4.10c is never picked up.

findings.location: docs/internal/product/backlog-notes.md:M4.10c block, the "OLD OBJECTS MUST STILL DECODE" paragraph
findings.title: The goldens a key change would touch are not named, and no gate sees a regenerated .bin
findings.failure_scenario: The row cites M3.0's precedent ("golden/segment-v0.bin is untouched, not regenerated") but never names the goldens THIS change would touch. All three exist in the tree: format/src/test/resources/golden/checkpoint-v0.bin, golden/chain-delta-v0.bin, golden/chain-delta-batched-v1.bin. MEASURED: scripts/test_integrity.py scores only Java assertion text (its STRENGTH table is regexes over assertX( and AssertJ chains) and TEST_PATH matches /src/test/java/ only, so a regenerated .bin resource is invisible to check-test-integrity.sh -- the one gate that exists for testing.md rule 5. A session that bumps the key shape, watches the golden round-trip fail, and regenerates the .bin to make it pass gets a green tree and has deleted the only evidence that pre-upgrade objects ever decoded. Naming the three files makes "untouched, not regenerated" checkable by a reader, since no script will do it. This also confirms what the parent asked me to check against the tree: BOTH delta goldens already exist, so the M4.10c claim "both paths change, or neither" is not merely a code fact -- a future golden must cover v0 and the kinded v1, and the fixtures for both are already sitting there.

findings.location: docs/internal/product/backlog-notes.md:M4.10d block, "Deleting that assertion instead is the testing.md rule 5 inversion"
findings.title: MEASURED: the tripwire the anchor leans on can be deleted with no gate firing
findings.failure_scenario: `doesNotContainKey` is absent from scripts/test_integrity.py's STRENGTH table, so it scores 0. Measured on the real body of theFirstCheckpointAfterATakeoverCarriesNoPodsAtAll (CheckpointWriterContentTest:145-157): current method strength 2; with the doesNotContainKey("poda") line DELETED, 2 -- no drop, so check-test-integrity.sh passes; with it INVERTED to containsEntry, 4. So the prescribed inversion is safely allowed by the gate (good), but the failure mode the row warns against -- deleting the tripwire rather than inverting it -- is unenforced, and the row reads as though a gate stood behind it. Remedy is rung 1 per gate-design and belongs to a separate task, not this commit: add doesNotContainKey|doesNotContain|doesNotContainEntry to the table. Minimum here: one clause in M4.10d saying no gate sees the deletion, so the implementer knows the sentence is the only guard.

findings.title: FakeSequencer is bound to "M4.10" by its own javadoc, and M4.10d never names it
findings.failure_scenario: FakeSequencer's javadoc (sequencer/src/testFixtures/.../FakeSequencer.java:27-29) promises idempotency on (podId, flushSeq) "lands here in the same commit as the real behaviour so the two cannot drift", and Sequencer's javadoc states the fake does not model it. Both name M4.10, which this commit sets to `split`. M4.10d, which is the commit that lands the real behaviour, never names FakeSequencer. If the fake is not updated in that commit, every test built on it keeps exercising a sequencer that duplicates on replay -- a fake that lies about the contract -- and two javadoc paragraphs in the tree become false in the non-negotiable-4 sense. The trail does resolve in one hop (M4.10 row -> split banner -> M4.10d), which is why this is minor rather than major; one clause in M4.10d naming FakeSequencer closes it.

findings.title: Inverting the assertion falsifies the test method's own name
findings.failure_scenario: The method is named theFirstCheckpointAfterATakeoverCarriesNoPodsAtAll. After the prescribed inversion it asserts the opposite -- the first checkpoint after a takeover DOES carry poda=42. A method whose name states the negation of what it asserts is read by the next session as a test that regressed and was papered over, which is the exact smell testing.md rule 5 exists to make visible. The row says "invert", not "invert and rename"; one word closes it.
